title: Fab City Index node report
description: PROPOSED FOR METHOD v1, IN REVIEW. What a lab or a city reports about the design and production nodes in one place: how many machines each has, who owns it, and where its models run. It is the only source of the two v1 indicators capacity_ownership_share and local_model_share (cells/*.yaml, `proposed_in`); the fablabs.io directory and Open Know-Where carry no owner field. Nothing reads these files until the method is accepted, and no reports/ folder exists yet. fci-index compute/v1_stubs.py checks the same rules in code, because a report comes from outside.

name.description: The lab, the city department, or the person who runs the node. A name someone can write back to.

id.description: Stable across reports: a later report for the same id replaces the earlier one. A fablabs.io slug where the node has one.

machines.description: Digital fabrication machines the node runs (laser cutters, CNC mills, 3D printers, vinyl and PCB machines, looms). A count, not a value: the v1 share weighs a machine as a machine.

owner_type.description: Who owns the machines. Local: local_public (a council, a public school or university of the place), cooperative, resident (people who live there), local_firm (a firm whose owners are in the place). Outside: outside_firm, outside_public (a national or foreign body). unknown is counted apart, never as outside.

model_runtime.description: Where the node's AI inference runs, if it runs any. local_hardware: on machines the node controls. open_weights_local: open-weight models the node can inspect and retrain, under its control. closed_api: a remote service whose model it cannot inspect. none: no model, and then the node is left out of local_model_share.

date.description: When this was true, YYYY-MM-DD. It ages like any measurement: full weight for two years, nothing at twelve.
